Digoxin is a positive inotrope used in heart failure. It works by blocking the Na+/K+ ATPase in the cardiomyocyte which causes a decrease in sodium movement into the cell. This in turn causes more sodium to be exchanged for calcium ions, causing an increase in intracellular calcium. This means that the heart can contract more strongly.

Aldosterone is a steroid hormone that is involved in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). It is released by the adrenal glands in response to decreased blood pressure. Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the kidneys, which increases blood pressure. It also increases the release of ADH, which increases water reabsorption by the kidneys, which also increases blood pressure.

Agranulocytosis is a severe form of neutropenia characterised by a marked reduction in the absolute neutrophil count. It is an undesirable side effect of certain drugs, most commonly clozapine. Clozapine should not be used in patients with a history of agranulocytosis or neutropenia. Patients on clozapine should be monitored for signs of agranulocytosis, particularly during the initial 1-2 months of treatment. Clozapine should not be stopped, although a dose reduction may be considered if agranulocytosis is suspected. If the neutropenia is mild, a dose reduction may be sufficient to prevent the development of agranulocytosis. If the neutropenia is severe, clozapine should be stopped and an alternative antipsychotic prescribed. A dose of clozapine may be restarted after 6-8 weeks when neutrophil counts have recovered.
